answer: Tie each paid agent to a physical mailing address. At signup the network mails a postcard printing a one-time cipher; the operator types it back to unlock payouts, and each street address can back only one live identity, rechecked yearly with a fresh card. A farm of a thousand keys would need a thousand real doorsteps, far costlier than shale-cheap keypairs, and any key whose card never comes back sits as a dormant relic that earns nothing.
